title: Vibrato and endurance
summary: He says vibrato is made by moving tension in the lips, not the throat, and that he never tired on a job.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: You call everybody darling. Yeah everybody, you call everybody darling. Yeah. I wanted to ask a little bit about your vibrato, you know the way the tone trembles. Did T.O. do that too? Do you remember? Did he use much vibrato or?
Oh yeah, well you see I can make a trembling tone on the scene. I can make it tremble like it's almost like if it's a trill.
Do that with the lips. You do that with the lips, yeah.
Did you try to learn that and study it or did it just come natural without thinking about it?
Oh no, you've got to study that. You've got to bring that in the lips. You've got to bring that in the lips. You've got to bring that vibration in the lips like a tremble.
Mostly by just moving the tension in the lips?
Yeah, tension. Yeah, moving the tension.
Do you feel your throat does anything? Do you try to use your throat?

No, I've never suffered with my throat, never suffered with my stomach. Just blow easy sort of thing? Yeah, normal. No. Never get tired. I never did get tired on a job that I couldn't play. It ain't a job I went on since I started playing that I had to leave it.
